text:
sam: heads up — noticed a flapping failure in CI when an atlantis apply runs while argocd is mid-sync. happened twice this week :grimacing:

rachel: ugh. symptoms? logs?

sam: short version: gha job renders kustomize, then atlantis plan -> apply. if argocd already rendered and expects secret refs mapped by our secret-sync job, the apply succeeds but argocd later fails to render and marks app OutOfSync. sometimes apply races with our secrets bootstrap and k8s secret creation. attached snippet from gha run:```
2026-03-08T14:12:03Z runner: kustomize build ./overlays/prod | kubectl apply --server-dry-run=client -f -
2026-03-08T14:12:08Z atlantis: apply started for module infra/k8s/services
2026-03-08T14:12:10Z secret-sync: creating secret myservice-prod from ssm://secret/path
2026-03-08T14:12:11Z kubernetes: resource deployed
2026-03-08T14:12:30Z argocd: app myservice failed to render: missing secret "myservice-prod"
```

ton y: can we gate atlantis apply until a separate preflight job confirms kustomize+secret mapping will be stable after argocd reconcile?

lina: +1. my suggestion: add a GH Actions job `ci-preflight-render` that runs `kustomize build`, validates with `kubeval`/`kube-apiext` and then runs a secret-check script that verifies entries exist in SSM and that our secret-sync operator has created the k8s secret in the target cluster (using `kubectl get secret -n ns myservice-prod --ignore-not-found`). pass/fail determines a PR status check.

sam: makes sense. we also need to avoid duplicate rendering differences (argocd vs gha). maybe we should render using the same kustomize/k8s versions argocd runs. we pin a container image for render step.

ci-bot: suggested job YAML snippet ->```yaml
jobs:
  ci-preflight-render:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/kustomize-runner:1.5.2
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: kustomize build overlays/prod > rendered.yaml
      - run: kubeval --kubernetes-version=1.25 rendered.yaml
      - run: ./scripts/check-secrets.sh rendered.yaml 
```

rachel: what does check-secrets.sh do?

ci-bot: pseudo:```bash
# check-secrets.sh rendered.yaml
for secret in $(yq e '.. | select(.kind=="Secret") | .metadata.name' rendered.yaml); do
  # map secret -> external store key using our mapping logic
  key=$(python -c "from mapping import map_secret; print(map_secret(''$secret''))")
  aws ssm get-parameter --name $key || { echo "missing $key"; exit 2; }
  # optionally probe cluster for k8s secret if kubeconfig present
  kubectl --context prod get secret $secret -n $NAMESPACE --ignore-not-found || echo "cluster-missing:$secret"
done
```

tony: couple of followups: 1) who provides kubeconfig in CI for cluster probe? 2) how do we signal atlantis to wait on this preflight?

lina: for probe we can use a read-only service account token stored in GH secrets (scoped to readonly), mounted as kubeconfig in the job. That token already exists for smoke tests (we can reuse). For atlantis, simplest approach: add a required branch protection check named `ci/preflight` (status context) and update our atlantis workflow so `atlantis apply` job depends on that check passing. Atlantis will still be triggered by comments, but our GH Actions gating will block merges/applies on protected branches.

sam: alternative is atlantis pre-apply hook. Atlantis supports `workflow` with `pre_apply` step that could call a script to poll status of preflight. downside: adding polling logic to Atlantis config and risk of long locks.

rachel: I prefer the GH status check + branch protection route. less change to atlantis infra and more visible in PR UI. Also lets us run the expensive secret probes only as part of PR check instead of every atlantis run.

tony: agree. we should also add an argocd health hook: if argocd reports missing secret, we post an annotation to the app with the missing key and a link to the PR so debugging is easier. small automation in argocd-sync controller.

lina: I'll draft the GH Actions job and the `check-secrets.sh` and post a PR today. will include an opt-in env var for clusters where we can't probe.

sam: thanks. once PR is up ping @rachel and @tony for quick review. after merge we need a short communication to SRE + platform so they know the new required status context for merges. :memo:

infra-bot: created checklist -> [ ] add `ci/preflight` as required check to repo protection; [ ] add job image to infra images; [ ] update atlantis docs; [ ] deploy argocd annotation helper

rachel: sounds good. small nit: ensure the job times out within 10m to avoid blocking other checks indefinitely.

lina: noted. will cap at 8m and fall back to `warning` status on timeout so it doesn't block emergency fixes.

sam: perfect. thanks everyone.

tony: :shipit:

rachel: thanks!
